samples.summary: `mergeInlineStyle`'s phantom-key deletion is untested for non-boolean clears (href / clear formatting)
samples.evidence: The block-helpers change replaces `{...inline.style, ...resolvedStyle}` with `mergeInlineStyle`, which additionally `delete`s keys whose patch value is `undefined`. The pre-existing removeLink test (document.test.ts:661-672) only asserts `style.href` is `toBeUndefined()`, which is equally true of the old plain spread (key present with value undefined), so it cannot detect a regression of the delete. The new toggle tests at lines 307-343 also do not distinguish: after normalizeInlines the three runs merge into the FIRST inline's copied style (block-helpers.ts:80-84 merges into `last`, whose style never had the key), so `'italic' in inlines[0].style === false` holds whether mergeInlineStyle deletes or leaves `italic: undefined`. Only the heading-6 test (line 345) — where the run does not merge because `italic: false` is kept — actually exercises the delete, and only for `bold`. Clear formatting (CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE), explicitly named in the new doc comment as a caller of this merge, has no test asserting the keys are absent rather than present-undefined.

samples.summary: The named-style exception in `styleOffAsClear` is untested for blocks inside table cells / header-footer, where `findBlock` can return undefined and silently fall back to `{}`
samples.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` resolves named-style defaults via `this.findBlock(blockId)` and falls back to `defaults = {}` when the block is not found; `findBlock` reaches cell blocks only through `_blockParentMap`, which document.ts:193-196 says is populated at layout time. The only test of the keep-`false` exception (document.test.ts:345, heading-6) uses a top-level body block. The changed cell-rectangle path (`applyInlineStyleToCellRectangle`) is covered only for plain paragraphs with `bold` (backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:636, 579), where the named-style branch never runs, and no test covers a heading (or any style-supplied italic) inside a table cell or header, nor the `block === undefined` fallback branch. So the branch documented as load-bearing ("clearing it would leave the run italic and the toggle-off would be a visual no-op") is unverified exactly where block lookup is most fragile.
searchedFor: Grep 'heading' usage in docs view toggle tests

samples.summary: The second stated motivation — a stored `false` pinning a run against a later named-style redefinition (lazy cascade, #749) — has no test
samples.evidence: The `styleOffAsClear` doc comment and the test's own header comment claim two harms: runs never re-merging (covered by the new tests at lines 307-343) and the dead flag pinning the run against "a style later redefined to set it" (the lazy-cascade hazard). No test in the diff or in the docs suite toggles a boolean off and then redefines the block's named style to verify the run now picks up the redefined value. I searched document.test.ts's applyInlineStyle/setBlockType blocks and grepped the docs tests for style-redefinition helpers and found none touching this sequence.

samples.summary: Optional-chaining assertions on `getBlock(...)` pass vacuously if the block disappears
samples.evidence: `expect(store.getBlock(block.id)?.inlines[0].style.bold).toBeUndefined()` (and the redo assertion) is satisfied when `getBlock` returns undefined, i.e. it cannot distinguish "flag cleared" from "block lost". The preceding `toBe(true)` assertions make this mostly harmless, but the negative assertions carry no existence check of their own; asserting on a non-optional local (e.g. a `const b = store.getBlock(...)!` plus `expect(b).toBeTruthy()`) would remove the escape hatch. The docs test at document.test.ts:363 (`'bold' in (cd?.style ?? {})`) has the same shape.
